text:
mika: Heads up — we just saw a spike of GPU node churn in eu-west-1 over the last 20m. Several model pods briefly 502'd while nodes were cycling. CA logs show a weird pattern: it first marks nodes as unneeded, then refuses to evict (PDB), then a few minutes later another scale-down removes a different node and the cycle repeats.

autoscaler-bot: Notice: cluster-autoscaler (v1.23.1) detected scale-down candidates: nodepool-gpu-eu-west-1a-*, reason: low utilization. Backoff window applied.

sasha: Can you paste the CA flags and a snippet of the logs you saw? Is this limited to preemptible/pool mixing?

mika: quick dump from the deployment args and a log excerpt: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=1m
--scale-down-delay-after-delete=1m
--scale-down-delay-after-failure=3m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--max-node-provision-time=15m
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
CA log: 
```
I0521 10:12:03 cluster.go:384] Node node-gn-17 marked unneeded (util 0.12)
I0521 10:12:04 eviction.go:210] Can't evict Pod(model-x-0): PodViolatesPDB
I0521 10:16:08 cluster.go:402] Node node-gn-22 marked unneeded (util 0.09)
I0521 10:17:01 scale_down.go:133] Removing node node-gn-22 (no evict reason)
```

mika: note the pools are heterogenous: mix of preemptible and reserved GPU SKUs across AZs, and several training jobs set PDB=1 for short-lived batches.

raj: Looks like two interacting signals: CA sees nodes with low CPU/GPU utilization but can't evict core pods because of PDBs -> leaves nodes running, then other nodes are chosen next and removed. That causes packing shuffle + short-term pressure. My advice: make CA less aggressive for GPU pools and make nodepool sizing more explicit.

anya: PDBs are respected by CA — there's no CA flag to ignore PDBs (for good reason). Options: increase --scale-down-unneeded-time, increase --scale-down-delay-after-add, or carve GPU pools into a separate autoscaler or set a higher min size for GPU pools so we never get below safe capacity. Also consider annotating long-lived training controllers with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false so CA won't count the node as reclaimable.

sasha: Agreed. Proposed quick mitigation for eu-west GPU pools: 
- bump --scale-down-unneeded-time from 10m -> 30m for GPU nodepools only
- bump --scale-down-delay-after-add 1m -> 10m to avoid removing recently provisioned nodes
- raise --scale-down-utilization-threshold 0.5 -> 0.65 (reduce aggressiveness)
- set nodepool min for preemptible pool to 2 (avoid complete empties)

ops-oncall: I'll run a canary patch in eu-west. Patch command I used before: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system set args deployment/cluster-autoscaler --containers=cluster-autoscaler \
  -- '--scale-down-unneeded-time=30m' '--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m' '--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.65'
```
(we're running autoscaler as a single global deployment today, so this will affect all pools — prefer a targeted approach next).

ops-oncall: Prometheus queries to monitor churn: 
```
rate(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="false"}[5m])
rate(cluster_autoscaler_scale_downs_total[5m])
sum by (nodepool) (rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m]))
```
Watch node eviction failures: 
```
{kubernetes_pod_event_reason="FailedEviction"} |~ "PodViolatesPDB"
```

raj: Long-term: split GPU workloads into two nodepools: 
- reserved-gpu for steady-state inference (min >= 2, small scale-up headroom)
- burst-gpu-preemptible for training (min 0, but with higher scale-down-unneeded-time and affinity to avoid kicking PDB-protected pods).
Also consider running a dedicated CA instance for GPU pools with tuned flags so we don't need global compromises.

mika: thanks — can we do the quick change as a global canary then follow with per-pool plan? I'll coordinate with infra change window.

anya: one extra note: network flaps increase node NotReady and can trick CA into thinking nodes are evictable/low-util; ops, can we confirm there were no underlying network interrupts in the same window?

ops-oncall: already checked: minor CNI errors at 10:10-10:14 that correlate with the first churn. I pushed an FYI to net-team. For now I'll roll the autoscaler args and keep an eye on Prometheus + alert noise.

sasha: TL;DR: quick fix = make CA less eager (increase unneeded-time, delay-after-add, and utilization threshold) + short-term min sizing for preemptible pools. Medium = separate CA or per-pool flags. Long = split workload types.

mika: cool, thanks everyone. I'll file a follow-up RFC for GPU pool split and dedicated CA. :rocket:

ops-oncall: rolling the args now, will report back in ~15m with metrics. :eyes:
